# We One Aviation Academy — LLM Index

DGCA pilot training academy in Dwarka, New Delhi, India. Operating since 2009. We teach the DGCA ground subjects for the written examinations behind a Commercial Pilot Licence, and we arrange flight training with partner flying schools in India, the USA, Canada, Australia and South Africa.

We are a ground school and a placement route into flying schools. We do not own aircraft or simulators, we do not employ pilots, and we do not place students into airline jobs — hiring decisions rest with the operator. What we provide is classroom teaching, examination preparation, licence-route planning, interview preparation and career guidance.

## Services

- **DGCA Ground Classes** — Classroom and online teaching for the five DGCA written papers: Air Navigation, Aviation Meteorology, Air Regulations, Technical General and Technical Specific. Roughly six months, with mock tests and live doubt sessions. https://weoneaviation.in/dgca-ground-classes
- **CPL preparation (Commercial Pilot Licence)** — The full route to the licence that lets a pilot be paid to fly: eligibility, the DGCA papers, and placement with a flying school for the 200 hours of flight time. https://weoneaviation.in/courses/cpl
- **PPL guidance (Private Pilot Licence)** — The recreational licence and the usual stepping stone to a CPL, since PPL hours count towards the commercial total. https://weoneaviation.in/ppl-full-form
- **SPL guidance (Student Pilot Licence)** — The first licence in the Indian chain, available from age 16, which permits flight training including solo flying under instructor authorisation. https://weoneaviation.in/student-pilot-license-spl
- **ATPL ground preparation** — Advanced theory for pilots already holding a CPL and building command experience towards airline command. https://weoneaviation.in/courses/atpl
- **RTR (A) preparation** — The Radio Telephone Operator (Restricted) certificate, examined separately from the DGCA papers under the Radio Telephone Operator (Restricted) Certificate and Licence Rules, 2025. https://weoneaviation.in/rtr-a
- **Flight-training placement abroad** — Routes through partner schools in the USA, Canada, Australia and South Africa, with DGCA conversion on return. https://weoneaviation.in/courses
- **Airline interview preparation** — Interview practice, licence-route planning and career guidance for pilots applying to operators. https://weoneaviation.in/airline-preparation-course

## Key Data

Minimum ages, set by the Aircraft Rules, 1937, Schedule II (continued in force by section 43(2) of the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024):

- Student Pilot Licence (SPL): **16 years** — Section B
- Private Pilot Licence (PPL, Aeroplanes): **17 years** — Section E
- Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL, Aeroplanes): **18 years** — Section J
- Airline Transport Pilot Licence (ATPL, Aeroplanes): **21 years** — Section M

CPL requirements, Schedule II Section J:

- Education: Class 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics from a recognised Board or University — para 1(b)
- Total flight time: **200 hours** as pilot of an aeroplane, flown within the **five years** immediately preceding the application — para 1(e)
- Inside that 200: 100 hours pilot-in-command, 20 hours cross-country as PIC (including one flight of at least 300 nautical miles with full-stop landings at two different aerodromes), 10 hours instrument time (at most 5 on an approved simulator), 5 hours night flying — paras 1(e)(i) to (iv)
- Medical: a certificate of physical fitness from an approved Medical Board — para 1(c)
- Radio: a current Flight Radio Telephone Operator Licence, RTR (A) — para 1(g)
- Skill test: flown for an examiner on the type applied for, within the six months before applying — para 1(h)

DGCA written papers for a CPL: Air Navigation, Aviation Meteorology, Air Regulations, Technical General, Technical Specific. RTR (A) is examined separately. Papers are cleared individually, not in a single sitting.

ATPL experience: the table in Schedule II Section M was amended by G.S.R. 22(E) of 7 January 2020 and again by G.S.R. 731(E) of 10 October 2023. Any hours figure from an older source may be out of date — confirm against the current notified Schedule.

DGCA Computer Number and exam booking (checked 11 September 2026 against the DGCA Pariksha FAQ, the Flight Crew User Manual Issue III Rev 0 of October 2024, the official rejection-reasons list and the Programme of Examinations 2026):

- TWO ROUTES since 16 October 2025. Registering through DigiLocker allots the computer number immediately on successful submission, and for the Class X and XII documents fetched from DigiLocker no Board Verification Certificate is required (public notice File No. DGCA-19012/47/2019-CEO-DGCA, 13 December 2024). The DigiLocker route needs Indian nationality, both certificates present in DigiLocker and an exactly matching Aadhaar; any mismatch sends the application back to the manual route. The BVC has not been abolished — it is waived only for documents DigiLocker supplies.
- The computer number is the identification number the Central Examination Organisation (CEO), DGCA — East Block III, Level III, R.K. Puram, New Delhi 110066 — allots for flight crew examinations, under Rule 41A of the Aircraft Rules, 1937.
- Apply online only, at pariksha.dgca.gov.in. Minimum age 16; no maximum age. Lifetime validity; one number per candidate. Issued within 15 working days of a complete application. No hard copy and no notary attestation for the computer number application (separately, the examination application PDF with documents must reach CEO for a new candidate).
- Education: every category other than PPL needs 10+2 passed with Physics and Mathematics; both the marksheet and the pass certificate are needed for Class 10 and Class 12.
- A Board Verification Certificate is mandatory for every new candidate for Class 10 and Class 12. Addressed to CEO or "To Whomsoever": processed on the original already being at CEO. Addressed to the flying school: upload a copy attested by the Chief Flying Instructor. Addressed to the candidate: attested or self-attested copy. Coloured photocopies are not accepted.
- Name exactly as on the Class 10 marksheet or the passport, whichever was issued later; a mismatch in basic details causes complete rejection. Date of birth proved only by the Class 10 certificate and marksheet or a birth certificate — not by Aadhaar.
- Uploads: photograph JPG up to 70 KB (45 × 35 mm, white background, face about 70%, under 3 months old); signature JPG up to 20 KB (20 × 45 mm); marksheets and pass certificates PDF up to 500 KB; date-of-birth, board verification, equivalence, address, Aadhaar and other certificates PDF up to 100 KB; logbook, passport and visa PDF up to 200 KB. Nothing can be added after Final Submit.
- Rejection: partial rejection is corrected under the same Temporary ID, a maximum of three times; complete rejection means applying again as a fresh applicant. Appeals go to the Director, CEO — ceo.dgca@nic.in, by post, or in person Tuesday and Thursday 3 PM to 5 PM.
- Examination fees: ₹2,500 per paper in a regular session, ₹5,000 per paper for an Online On-Demand Examination (OLODE), ₹500 per oral paper for the second and third attempt only. Payment through Bharatkosh only, completed by 2300 hrs on the closing date; no change or refund once submitted. One application per session, two centre choices, one specific-aircraft paper per session.
- 2026 sessions, published by DGCA as tentative — regular: 10–14 March, 16–20 June, 22–26 September, 15–19 December. OLODE: 21–23 January, 4–6 February, 22–24 April, 20–22 May, 15–17 July, 19–21 August, 28–30 October, 18–20 November.
- Full sourced guide: https://weoneaviation.in/dgca-computer-number

DGCA medical, Class 1 and Class 2 (checked 11 September 2026 against Aircraft Rules 1937 rules 39B and 39C, CAR Section 7 Series 'C' Part I Rev. 6 of 18 October 2022, and DGCA's list of approved centres updated 27 August 2026):

- Class 1 is required for the Commercial Pilot Licence and the Airline Transport Pilot Licence (aeroplane and helicopter), and for a Private Pilot Licence where instrument rating privileges are required. Valid one year up to age 60, six-monthly thereafter; six-monthly above 40 for single-crew operations.
- Class 2 is required for the Private Pilot Licence, microlight pilot licence, the Student Pilot Licence in all its forms, and Flight Radio Telephone Operator Licences. Valid two years up to age 50, one year thereafter.
- Class 3 is for air traffic controller licences: four years up to 40, two years from 40 to 50, one year above 50.
- Rule 39C was amended on 27 December 2019 to raise the age limit for Class 1 validity from forty years to sixty. Sources still placing the six-monthly band at 40 are quoting the pre-2020 rule.
- Class 1 is conducted at Air Force medical centres, approved civil medical centres and by DGCA-empanelled Class 1 examiners; Class 2 also by Class 2 examiners holding an MBBS with approved aviation medicine training.
- DGCA listed 13 approved centres as of 27 August 2026 — 3 Air Force and 10 civil. Four are in Delhi and the NCR: AFCME New Delhi, Indraprastha Apollo New Delhi, Max Multi Specialty Centre New Delhi, and Medanta in Gurugram.
- The examination covers physical and mental, visual and colour perception, and hearing, against ICAO Annex 1 Chapter 6 paragraphs 6.3.2 to 6.3.4. No pass rate is published.
- A computer number and the written examinations need no medical certificate. Full sourced guide: https://weoneaviation.in/dgca-class-2-class-1-medical

DGCA examination pass marks (CAR Section 7, Series 'B', Part I, Rev. 2 of 13 February 2019): 70% in the theoretical knowledge examination of each subject, per subject, not an aggregate (para 5.6). Oral examinations: 50% for SPL and Glider, 70% for ATPL and the instructor ratings (para 5.7). A failed first ATPL oral allows two further chances within two years. Passed papers must fall within two and a half years before the licence application, except for CPL and ATPL where the period is five years (para 6.7).

Academy facts: founded 2009; located at C-404, 3rd Floor, Ramphal Chowk, Block C, Palam Extension, Sector-7, Dwarka, New Delhi 110077; phone +91-9667370747; email info.weoneaviation@gmail.com.
